newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait bourse index hits record high in busy week.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait bourse index hits record high in busy week.

text.p: Kuwait share index ended the week to Wednesday hitting a new peak as healthy economic indicators and signs of good performance by listed firms fuelled active trade, dealers said on Thursday.
"The economy is showing good improvement. That along with stability are very important factors behind increased activity and prices," said Mansour Jasem, a private dealer.
Kuwait has earned 731 billion dinars more than forecast in the first half of the current fiscal year to end-June, Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan has said.
The proposed state budget for 1997/98 shows a deficit fall to 1.17 billion dinars compared to 1.21 billion in the current year, figures released earlier this week show.
Also, "so far many listed firms are doing very well," said another dealer.
The index finished the week at 2,336.6, a rise of 39.3 points compared to last week. Losers led gainers 29-25, while 12 shares were non-movers.

"There is no real investment opportunities to attract the capital held by private investors, which surfaces at the exchange. That also applies to capital from neighbouring Gulf countries," said an economist.

The daily average for value of traded shares rose to a record 99.4 dinars ($327 million) from 67 million. Volume rose to a daily average of 345 million shares from 234 million, also a record high, figures released by the Kuwait Stock Exchange on Thursday show.
Investment firms were the most active sector in terms of traded value with 206 million dinars, followed by real estate firms with 191 million and banks with 44 million.
United Realty, Kuwait Real Estate, Investment Projects, National Investment and Gulf Bank were among the most active shares.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest in mutual funds.
